claim.summary: One-sided density with the Fejer kernel, N simple off-line pairs at heights gamma_0 + j pi/L and one distance delta, b = delta L: |P(x - L)| <= 1/cos(pi x/(2L)) for 0 <= x < L and |G(tau)| <= (1 + 3 pi^2/(2 b^2) + N (1 + b/2) e^(-b/2))/delta^2 for all tau, so at this length N = o(e^(b/2)/b) simple pairs give a negative part no larger than 1 + o(1) times one pair's bound.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the exponential sum is a geometric series with ratio -e^(-i pi x/L). An upper bound at the resonant length only.

claim.summary: One-sided density with the Fejer kernel: for k+1 off-line pairs at heights gamma_0 + j pi/L with multiplicities binom(k, j) at one distance delta, |G| <= (k+1)! (pi/b)^k/delta^2 and D_off >= -(2 e^b/(L delta^2)) (k+1)! (pi/b)^k - 6 * 2^k/(L delta^2); with real points on a lattice of spacing s <= 2 pi/L the whole density is nonnegative once 2 pi/s is at least that bound, which for k = floor(b/pi) is at most (2 e^2/(L delta^2)) (b/pi + 1)^(3/2) e^((1 - 1/pi) b) + 6 * 2^(b/pi)/(L delta^2).
claim.assessment: Working proof: the exponential sum is (1 + q)^k with |1 + q| <= pi x/L. With real density l/(2 pi), for each length with b up to about 1.47 log l (asymptotically) the cluster built for that length is hidden at it, where a single pair shows from about log l; its multiplicities are at most l^0.32 there. One cluster per length; not shown that a fixed cluster hides at shorter lengths, that the family shows soon after, or that no admissible cluster hides longer.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.next_action: Decide whether a family with bounded multiplicities hides up to lengths of order log T.

claim.assessment: Working proof from the gap-free power sum bound applied at n sample points. The bound counts every off-line pair of the configuration, not those near one height, and through the earlier constant gives sup Re G only of order (2 e b)^(-6n).

claim.summary: Fejer kernel K_L(w) = 2(1 - cos Lw)/(L w^2), off-line pairs gamma_j -+ i delta with multiplicities m_j, b = delta L: the off-line part of the density sum_z m_z K_L(tau - z) equals -(2 e^b/L) Re G(tau) + E(tau) with G(tau) = sum m_j e^{-iL(tau - gamma_j)}/(tau - gamma_j + i delta)^2, |E| <= 6 Y/L, Y = sum m_j/((tau - gamma_j)^2 + delta^2); G(tau) = -int_0^inf x e^{-delta x} P(x - L) e^{i(x-L) tau} dx with P(y) = sum m_j e^{-iy gamma_j}; and the real points contribute at most (7/3) L N(2 pi/L), N a local count.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the complex cosine split into its growing and decaying exponentials, a Laplace transform identity, and a count of real points by distance in units of 2 pi/L.

claim.summary: In the setting of the one-sided density decomposition, with theta_j = L(gamma_j - gamma_1), k the number of vanishing moments sum m_j e^{iL gamma_j} theta_j^r and c_k = sum m_j |theta_j|^k: |G(tau)| <= (k+1) c_k/(delta^2 b^k) for all tau, so the negative part of the off-line density is at most (2 e^b/L)(k+1) c_k/(delta^2 b^k) + 6M/(L delta^2).
claim.assessment: Working proof: Taylor expansion of the exponential sum at the endpoint, as in the endpoint moment order. The one-sided density loses the power b^(-k) at the lengths where the second moment loses b^(-2k).

claim.assessment: Working proof: the pair's own term evaluated at a shift of pi/L, the others bounded by their distances. With a local count of order log T the threshold is b about log log T, a hypothesis on zeros not read in a source.

claim.summary: In the setting of the endpoint moment order with heights in increasing order: k = n-1 if and only if every gap is an odd multiple of pi/Lam and m_j is proportional to the product over l != j of 1/|gamma_j - gamma_l| (the divided-difference weights); if all heights lie in an open interval of length pi/Lam then k = 0.
claim.assessment: Working proof: the solution space of n-1 vanishing moments is spanned by the divided-difference weights, real with alternating signs, and positive multiplicities with unimodular phases match them exactly when consecutive phases are opposite.

claim.summary: For complex z_1..z_N with |z_j| >= 1 (not necessarily distinct), complex b_j, s_nu = sum b_j z_j^nu and m >= 0: the maximum of |s_nu| over m < nu <= m + N is at least |b_1 + ... + b_N| / A(m,N), A(m,N) = sum over k < N of binom(m+k,k) 2^k <= 2^(N-1) binom(m+N, N-1), and A <= (2e(m+N)/N)^N for m >= N-1.
claim.assessment: Working elementary proof by Newton interpolation of z^-(m+1), with divided differences expressed through complete homogeneous polynomials. Recalled by a reviewer as Turan's first main theorem with a later constant; neither read. For a cluster of n off-axis pairs it gives |S(s)| >= 2M e^{-delta_1 s}/A at one of 2n consecutive lattice points, with the exponential of the wrong sign, so in the goal's parameter it is below the trivial size and detects nothing.

claim.summary: In the setting of the one-sided density decomposition, with H_jl = 2/(2 delta + i(gamma_j - gamma_l))^3, J = int_0^inf x^2 e^{-2 delta x} |P(x - L)|^2 dx >= lambda_min(H) sum m_j^2 > 0, A1 = pi delta^2 J/M, eps = 2 pi L e^{-b} M and W the span of the heights: sup_tau Re G >= (A1/4 - eps/2)/(W + 16 M/A1); the lower bound for J does not depend on L, so no cluster makes the off-line part of the density nonnegative at arbitrarily large lengths.
claim.assessment: Working proof: Plancherel for G, nonnegativity of the integral of G^2, the integral of G by inversion, and the decay of G away from the heights. The constant is of order J^2 and far from sharp (ratios 10^2 to 10^10 in the control); no lower bound for lambda_min(H) under a local count is obtained.
